label: Population
note: 1 January 2026, estimated. Up 706,000 on a year earlier.
source: Eurostat ddn-20260710-3 (10 July 2026), dataset demo_gind

label: In the euro area
note: Bulgaria joined on 1 January 2026 and is the twenty-first.
source: European Commission IP/25/1386; European Central Bank

label: HICP inflation
note: June 2026, down from 3.3% in May. The euro area read 2.8%.
source: Eurostat 2-17072026-ap (17 July 2026), dataset prc_hicp_manr

label: Unemployment
note: June 2026, seasonally adjusted — 13.317 million people. The euro area read 6.3%. Stable both month on month and year on year.
source: Eurostat 3-30072026-bp (30 July 2026), dataset une_rt_m

label: ECB deposit facility rate
note: Raised 25 basis points on 11 June 2026, effective 17 June — the first rise after the 2025 cutting cycle — and held on 23 July. Main refinancing 2.40%, marginal lending 2.65%.
source: European Central Bank monetary policy decisions

label: Intra-EU trade in goods
note: What member states sell to each other. Reported on the dispatches basis and counted once here.
source: Eurostat 6-13022026-bp (13 February 2026), EU27, full-year 2025, provisional

label: Extra-EU exports of goods
note: What the Union as a whole sells to the rest of the world.
source: Eurostat 6-13022026-bp, EU27, full-year 2025, provisional

label: Extra-EU imports of goods
note: What it buys from the rest of the world. The extra-EU goods balance is a surplus of EUR 133.5bn.
source: Eurostat 6-13022026-bp, EU27, full-year 2025, provisional

label: United States
note: The largest partner on both flows combined, and the EU's largest surplus: EUR 198.4bn.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, Eurostat COMEXT statistical regime 4, extracted 20 May 2026

label: China
note: The largest single source of imports, and the EU's largest deficit by a wide margin: EUR 360.6bn.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: United Kingdom
note: Still the third largest partner six years after leaving, and the second largest destination for EU exports.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: Switzerland
note: A country of 9 million is the EU's fourth largest goods partner — larger than Japan and South Korea combined.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: Türkiye
note: In a customs union with the EU for industrial goods since 1995.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: Norway
note: The EU imports considerably more from Norway than it sells there — energy is most of the difference.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: Japan
note: Close to balanced.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: South Korea
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: India
note: Import value only. The factsheet table does not carry India's export figure, so the bar shows imports and the total is stated separately as EUR 118.4bn.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

label: Brazil
note: Neither flow is in the extracted table. Total trade EUR 87.1bn.
source: DG TRADE factsheet, COMEXT extracted 20 May 2026

source: Eurostat, World trade in goods and services — an overview
